title: Equations and formulas you will actually use
hook: A heater's element is 23 Ω and it gives out 2300 W. P = I²R tells you the power from the current, so how do you turn it round to find the current it draws?
oneBreath: An equals sign says both sides are the same amount, like a balance that sits level, not that the answer comes next. Do the same thing to both sides and it stays level, so x + 7 = 12 becomes x = 5 by taking 7 off each side. An equation such as 3x + 5 = 26 is a list of steps done to x, times 3 then add 5, and you solve it by undoing those steps in reverse: take 5 off, then divide by 3. When the unknown sits on both sides, take the same number of x's off both first, then finish the same way. A formula such as V = IR is an equation with letters for its numbers, so you can put in the numbers you know and solve for the one you don't. Changing a formula's subject is the same undoing done with letters, so V = IR turns into R = V ÷ I, and the undo for a square is a square root.

ideas.title: The balance
ideas.oneLine: = means both sides are the same amount, so do the same to both and it stays level: x + 7 = 12 gives x = 5.

ideas.title: Undo in reverse
ideas.oneLine: 3x + 5 = 26 is times 3 then add 5, so undo the last step first: take 5 off, then divide by 3.

ideas.title: Unknowns on both sides
ideas.oneLine: Take the same x's off both sides, so 5x + 2 = 3x + 10 becomes 2x + 2 = 10, then finish as before.

ideas.title: Using formulas
ideas.oneLine: Put the numbers you know into V = IR, P = VI or P = I²R and solve for the one you don't, or write the equation from the job.

ideas.title: Rearranging formulas
ideas.oneLine: Make another letter the subject by undoing the formula's steps, as V = IR becomes R = V ÷ I, and "change side, change sign" fails for × and ÷.

ideas.title: Rearranging harder formulas
ideas.oneLine: Undo a square with a square root in P = I²R, turn p1V1 = p2V2 round at absolute pressure, and find a cable's longest run from its mV/A/m.

calibration.why: Undo the last step first: 27 − 6 = 21, then 21 ÷ 3 = 7, and 3 × 7 + 6 = 27 checks. 11 adds the 6 instead of taking it off, and 3 divides the 27 but not the 6.

calibration.q: V = IR. Which one gives the current I?
calibration.why: I is multiplied by R, so divide both sides by R. V − R is the "change side, change sign" slip, which only works for + and −, and V × R does the step again instead of undoing it.
